extended_summary: ManifestStore provides centralized, atomic I/O operations for pipeline manifests with strict namespace separation between provenance metadata (model info, timing, quality) and worker hash manifests. ResumeStrategy provides static methods for pipeline resume point detection and coverage gap analysis. It determines where to start or resume a pipeline run by scanning manifest files on disk, handling complex edge cases like stub manifests from auto-recovery systems, shared output files between stages, and mtime-based freshness checks. The class implements sophisticated logic to distinguish between truly complete stages and false positives from inherited or stubbed data, preventing infinite restart loops while ensuring stages that actually need to run are not skipped.

The scheduler tracks per-node load, handles queueing when nodes are at capacity, and implements recovery mechanisms for idle slots.

It replaces an ad-hoc enum-based approach with explicit states (IDLE, QUEUED, RUNNING, PAUSING, PAUSED, CANCELLING, CANCELLED, COMPLETED, FAILED, RECOVERING), guarded transitions defined in a transition table, and comprehensive event handling for normal progression, queuing, pausing, cancellation, and crash recovery scenarios. The state machine coordinates with stage snapshots for progress tracking and supports complex workflows including between-stage queuing when compute capacity is unavailable.
